pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: app/referendum/og/route.tsx:38 Both OG renderers take a URL out of the body of the Google Fonts CSS response with a regex and fetch it from the server. Nothing checks the scheme, host or resolved address, redirects are followed automatically, and the referendum copy has no time or size bound. This is the exact 'destination arrives inside a dependency's response' case the technique calls attacker-controlled input.

techniques.evidence: app/graf/p/[ref]/opengraph-image.tsx:62 The URL is pulled from upstream CSS (line 60 regex). There is no scheme or host allowlist, no check on the resolved address, no manual redirect handling and no response-size bound. A time bound exists here but not in app/referendum/og/route.tsx:35/38, which has neither a timeout nor validation.
app/graf/p/[ref]/opengraph-image.tsx:58 The only external upstream these routes reach is a public, credential-free font host. No privileged upstream is brokered and no secret is attached.

app/graf/p/[ref]/bundle/route.ts:23 Closed vocabulary 404/410/503 with null bodies. A store outage is a retryable 503, kept apart from not-found (lines 16-21), so failure never reads as an empty success, and no store detail crosses back.

features/graph/getPermalinkData.ts:29 No process.env or NEXT_PUBLIC value is read in this context's files. The server-only marker sits in the loader module the permalink page, OG image and bundle route import, so the module itself is guarded (mark the module, not the entry point).

app/referendum/page.tsx:44 The browser holds no data-store credential. The server computes the anonymous vote aggregate and passes only that as props, so there is no regime-one view or grant to judge.
app/graf/page.tsx:30 The browser reaches graph rows only through server actions. No store row-policy engine faces a browser role.
app/graf/page.tsx:29 No table is readable by a public role. The page ships only a server-shaped seed of kind counts and entry points.

app/graf/p/[ref]/page.tsx:13 The ref the browser carries back is re-derived on the server rather than trusted, which is the technique's own 'cheaply re-derive' exception. Nothing the client submits is acted on as a pass.
app/rentgen/page.tsx:23 The terminal renders review decisions and change events, not requests that carried credentials. There is no debug or log stream of credentialed traffic.

pairs.registryProposal: outbound-fetch-destination-validation could name the 'trusted CDN indirection' case. A fixed, deployment-configured first hop (a font CSS API) returns the address of a second hop (a font file). The 'destination fixed by the deployment' exception covers only the first hop. The proportionate rule is probably a pinned host-and-scheme allowlist on the second hop plus no redirects, a time bound and a size bound, not full resolve-and-pin machinery.
